label: lf-verify-regs
topic: Independent re-check of the key claims in tracks/research/agents/lf-fire-regs.json (fire-test regulations, test-capacity bottleneck, bio-based flame-retardant numbers)
summary: I re-fetched 12 of the cited sources on 2026-11-13 and compared them with the claims. Ten claims are SUPPORTED as written: Euroclass thresholds A1 to E, ASTM E84 classes, UL 94 V ratings, ISO 5660-1 status, EN 16623 stage, the UK capacity shortage, the USD 0.5-1M test program, both phytic-acid cotton papers' headline numbers and the mycelium cone numbers. Two are PARTLY supported. (1) The UK Approved Document B claim is out of date against the gov.uk page as I read it: the page now lists the 2019 edition incorporating 2020, 2022, 2025 AND 2026 amendments, collated with the 2029 amendments, and says withdrawal of the national classes (BS 476) "is concluded"; the original said the 2026 amendments were not yet collated and that withdrawal was still in transition. (2) In the Magovac phytic-acid paper the 57.0% pHRR reduction for 8 bilayers was not confirmed in my fetch; the page extract gave 59.5% (10 BL), 62.3% (12 BL), 63.3% (15 BL) and the text '~61%'. The instrument is microscale combustion calorimetry, not a cone calorimeter, which the original states only in the value field. One further caveat: in Zilke et al. the uncoated MCC pHRR of 216 W/g equals the HRC figure in the same table and may be a typo in the paper. Not re-checked for lack of time: DIN EN 13381-8 page, NFPA 285 article, NAHB page, CFPA-E notice, European Accreditation page, the Liang 2023 review, and all snippet-only claims (these stay unverified). All fetches went through a summarising fetch tool, so quotes are as returned by that tool, not from raw page bytes. No files were written.

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: Euroclass A1 needs dT<=30 C, mass loss<=50%, no sustained flaming, PCS<=2.0 MJ/kg; A2 dT<=50 C, tf<=20 s, PCS<=3.0 MJ/kg.
findings.confidence: high for the numbers; edition of EN 13501-1 behind them still not confirmed

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: Euroclass B FIGRA<=120 W/s, THR600s<=7.5 MJ, LFS < specimen edge, Fs<=150 mm in 60 s (30 s exposure); C 250 W/s and 15 MJ; D 750 W/s; E Fs<=150 mm in 20 s (15 s exposure).

SUPPORTED: ASTM E84 Class A FSI 0-25, B 26-75, C 76-200, SDI max 450; specimen 24 in x 24 ft; 10 minute test. Edition year not on the page (a link slug hints at 2024; the original's 'E84-25 from memory' stays unverified).
findings.evidence_quote: The actual fire test runs for 10 minutes.
findings.confidence: high for numbers (lab explainer, not the standard); edition unverified

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: UL 94 V-0 <=10 s per specimen, <=50 s total for five, afterglow <=30 s, no cotton ignition; V-1 <=30 s, <=250 s, <=60 s, no cotton ignition; V-2 same times, cotton ignition allowed.
findings.confidence: medium (secondary explainer, not the UL standard text)

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: ISO 5660-1:2015 (corrected version 2021-01) with Amd 1:2019 dated 2019-08-06 as newest item; no replacement edition named on the catalogue page.
findings.evidence_quote: specifies a method for assessing the heat release rate and dynamic smoke production rate

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: EN 16623:2015 is at stage 90.20 (under periodical review) dated 2026-07-15 and points to EN 13381-6, EN 13381-8 and prEN 13381-9 without fixing a required level. The original's evidence quote is a paraphrase stitched from two page phrases, not one verbatim sentence.
findings.evidence_quote: which are currently EN 13381-6, EN 13381-8 and prEN 13381-9

findings.claim: PARTLY: UK Approved Document B. The gov.uk page as fetched now lists the 2019 edition incorporating 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments, collated with 2029 amendments. The original said 2026 and 2029 were published but not yet collated, and that BS 476 national classes 'are being withdrawn'; the page now says the withdrawal is concluded.
findings.evidence_quote: 2019 edition incorporating 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments collated with 2029 amendments
findings.confidence: medium (the page has a long update history; the older 2024 note quoted by the original may also still be on it, I did not see it)

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: ICC posted final action results for the 2024-2026 Group A and B cycle on 2026-07-22; codes to be published later in 2026; appeal deadline 2026-08-13. The NAHB page and the 'IBC in September 2026' detail were not re-checked.

SUPPORTED: A UK fire-test provider states a lack of UKAS-accredited capacity, mentions three furnaces, a GBP 23m facility 80% larger, due early 2025; article dated 2024-02-23; no lead times in weeks. It is the provider's own commercial statement.
findings.evidence_quote: manufacturers are facing a lack of UKAS-accredited testing capacity today
findings.confidence: high that it was said; low as independent evidence of a bottleneck

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: Full-scale US mass-timber apartment fire test program cost about USD 500,000 to 1 million, much of it funded by the American Wood Council; article dated 2017-08-16.
findings.evidence_quote: the cost will be about $500,000 to $1 million

findings.claim: PARTLY: Magovac et al. 2020 phytic-acid layer-by-layer cotton. Confirmed: untreated LOI 18-19%, 8 BL 26%, 15 BL 31%; add-on 12.36-20.12%; 10, 12, 15 BL pass the vertical flame test with no afterflame; pHRR -59.5% (10 BL), -62.3% (12 BL), -63.3% (15 BL), about 61% average. NOT confirmed in my fetch: the 57.0% figure for 8 BL. The pHRR is from microscale combustion calorimetry, not a cone calorimeter.
findings.value: LOI 18-19 -> 26 -> 31%; pHRR -59.5 to -63.3% (MCC) confirmed; -57.0% at 8 BL unconfirmed
findings.evidence_quote: Cotton treated with 10, 12 or 15 BL reduces pHRR by ~61%
findings.confidence: high for confirmed values; the 8 BL value may simply not have been returned by the fetch extract

findings.claim: SUPPORTED (with caveat): Zilke et al. 2020 phytic acid / polyvinylamine coating. MCC pHRR 216 vs 42.8 W/g, THR 10.7 vs 4.2 kJ/g, TGA residue at 700 C under nitrogen 8.7% vs 29.1%, 15 BL add-on 18.8% with 2.0% P and 1.4% N, uncoated burns down in 64 s vs 0 s afterflame; LOI not reported. Caveat: the 216 W/g uncoated pHRR equals the HRC value in the same table and may be a typo in the paper. Also 10 BL has lower THR (3.0 kJ/g) than 15 BL (4.2), so the trend is not monotonic.
findings.confidence: high that the paper prints these; medium on the 216 W/g baseline itself

findings.claim: SUPPORTED: Jones et al. 2018 mycelium composites in the cone calorimeter at 50 kW/m2: about 200 kW/m2 peak for the 0-day control and about 180 for 6-18 day composites; residue about 23 wt% at 600 C vs 19 wt% for wheat grain. The exact title, which the original left as 'inferred', is now confirmed.
findings.value: pHRR ~200 vs ~180 kW/m2; residue 23 vs 19 wt%
findings.evidence_quote: marginally higher (ca. 10%) for the 0-d sample (200 kW/m2)
findings.confidence: high; note the improvement is only about 10%, so 'mycelium is fire-safe' is not what this shows

findings.claim: SUPPORTED (key claim 1, as logic): the regulatory grades are defined in SBI, tunnel and burn-time units, while the fetched bio-based papers report LOI, MCC and cone numbers; neither re-checked paper reports a Euroclass or E84 result.
findings.value: Euroclass B: FIGRA<=120 W/s, THR600s<=7.5 MJ; papers: LOI, MCC pHRR
findings.confidence: medium (an absence claim over only three papers)

findings.claim: COULD_NOT_FETCH (not attempted in the time budget): EN 13381-8 DIN page, NFPA 285 / IBC 2024 article, NAHB page, CFPA-E Nordic lab notice, European Accreditation 17025/17065 page, Liang 2023 wood review LOI 37.2% and 31.8%, and all search-snippet-only chitosan, alginate, lignin and polyamide numbers.
findings.confidence: none; these claims keep whatever status the original gave them, and the snippet-only ones should stay low

key_claims: Of 13 claims re-fetched, 11 are supported as written and 2 are partly supported; none were contradicted outright.
The UK Approved Document B entry is stale: the gov.uk page now shows the 2026 amendments incorporated and collated with 2029, and the BS 476 national-class withdrawal described as concluded.
The 57.0% pHRR reduction at 8 bilayers (Magovac 2020) was not confirmed; the confirmed range is 59.5-63.3% for 10-15 bilayers, measured by microscale calorimetry, not cone.
The bottleneck evidence is real but thin: one provider's own press statement and one cost figure for a single program from 2017.
Seven sources and all snippet-only numbers were not re-checked and remain unverified by this pass.
lay_summary: I opened twelve of the web pages the first report relied on and checked whether they really say what the report claimed.
Almost everything matched: the fire-grade numbers for Europe and the US, the lab company saying there are not enough approved test slots in the UK, and the plant-based coating results on cotton.
Two things did not fully match: the UK building guidance page has been updated since the wording in the report, and one percentage for a thin coating could not be found on the page.
Some pages I did not have time to open, so those claims are still unchecked.
The plant-based results are from tiny lab tests, which are not the tests that building rules use.

glossary.Euroclass: The European letter grade (A1 best, F worst) for how a building material reacts to fire.
glossary.FIGRA: Fire growth rate from the European corner test, in watts per second; lower is better.
glossary.THR600s: Total heat given off in the first 600 seconds of that corner test.
glossary.LFS: Lateral flame spread: how far sideways the flame travels across the test panel.
glossary.Fs: Flame spread height in the small-flame test, in millimetres.
glossary.PCS: Gross calorific potential: how much heat a kilogram of material can release when fully burned.
glossary.SBI: Single Burning Item test (EN 13823): a corner of two panels lit by a gas burner.
glossary.ASTM E84: US tunnel test that gives a flame spread index and a smoke index for surface materials.
glossary.FSI / SDI: Flame Spread Index and Smoke Developed Index, the two scores from ASTM E84.
glossary.UL 94: A small vertical burn test for plastics; V-0 is the strictest of the V ratings.
glossary.Afterflame / afterglow: How long a sample keeps flaming or glowing after the test flame is taken away.
glossary.LOI: Limiting oxygen index: the lowest oxygen percentage at which a material keeps burning; higher is safer.
glossary.pHRR: Peak heat release rate: the highest rate at which a burning sample gives off heat.
glossary.THR: Total heat released by a sample during a test.
glossary.HRC: Heat release capacity, another number from the microscale test, in different units from pHRR.
glossary.MCC: Microscale combustion calorimetry: a heat-release test on a few milligrams of material.
glossary.Cone calorimeter: A bench test (ISO 5660) that heats a small square of material and measures the heat it gives off.
glossary.TGA residue: What fraction of a sample is left after slow heating in a furnace balance; more residue means more char.
glossary.Layer-by-layer (LbL) / bilayer (BL): A coating built by dipping fabric alternately in two solutions; each pair of dips is one bilayer.
glossary.Add-on: How much weight the coating adds to the fabric, as a percentage.
glossary.Phytic acid: A phosphorus-rich compound from seeds and grains used as a plant-based flame retardant.
glossary.Mycelium: The root-like body of a fungus, grown through grain or straw to make a material.
glossary.UKAS: The UK body that officially approves test laboratories.
glossary.ISO/IEC 17025 and 17065: International rule sets for approved test labs (17025) and for product certification bodies (17065).
glossary.Approved Document B: The official fire-safety guidance for buildings in England.
glossary.BS 476: The older British fire test standards that the Euroclass system replaces.
glossary.Stage 90.20: A standards-body status code meaning the standard is under its routine periodic review.
glossary.Collated: Amendments merged into one combined document.

recommendations: Update the Approved Document B row and finding in lf-fire-regs.json: 2026 amendments are now incorporated, collated with 2029, and the BS 476 withdrawal is described as concluded; re-open the page to confirm exact wording before editing.
Re-open Table 3 of Magovac 2020 to confirm or drop the 57.0% (8 bilayer) pHRR figure, and move 'microscale calorimetry' from the value field into the claim text so it is not read as cone data.
Flag the Zilke 216 W/g uncoated pHRR as possibly a table typo (it equals the HRC value) before using it as a baseline.
Fix the EN 16623 evidence quote so it is a verbatim fragment rather than a stitched paraphrase.
Run a second verification pass on the seven sources not re-checked here, and keep snippet-only numbers out of any nanopublication.
